nodes.name: AirNet
nodes.description: The US domestic airport network as an explorable graph — surfacing hub structure, degrees of separation, and how the network degrades when its most connected airports are removed.

nodes.name: Nerdplexity
nodes.description: Analytics-first chat client for cloud and local LLMs — conversation quality and performance insights layered over a minimal React/Node chat UI running local inference through Ollama.

nodes.name: Observability
nodes.description: Making system and agent behavior inspectable after the fact.

nodes.name: LexOrchestrator
nodes.description: Litigation workflow agent: a legal drafting request moves through eight sequential specialist agents, grounded in hybrid RAG over indexed court opinions, with every citation checked back against the source and every run inspectable in a trace viewer.

nodes.name: Hybrid Retrieval
nodes.description: Combining keyword, vector, and authority signals in a single ranking pass.

nodes.name: MCP / Tool Interfaces
nodes.description: Exposing and instrumenting tools for agents over the Model Context Protocol.

nodes.name: Citation Verification
nodes.description: Checking generated claims against the sources they cite.

nodes.name: Mirofish Swarm API
nodes.description: A monetized prediction API over a multi-agent swarm: 10-500 agents with distinct roles debate a question across several rounds and return a structured prediction report, metered per call with on-chain USDC payments.
nodes.contributionNote: Original API and productization layer around the upstream MiroFish swarm engine — the Railway-deployable service, the x402/USDC payment gating, and the structured prediction report format are mine; the simulation engine itself is upstream work.

nodes.name: Multi-Agent Simulation
nodes.description: Running populations of agents to observe emergent outcomes.

nodes.name: GTM Simulator
nodes.description: A go-to-market simulation lab built on the upstream MiroFish swarm engine: enter a product brief, ICP, and messaging strategy, and get back generated buyer personas, simulated message reactions, ranked objections, and a seven-day outbound experiment plan.
nodes.contributionNote: Forked from the upstream MiroFish swarm-simulation engine. My work is the GTM productization layer: buyer-persona generation, message reaction simulation, objection ranking, the outbound experiment planner, and the deployed web app — not the underlying simulation engine, which is upstream work.

Grew out of the public LexOrchestrator demo.

nodes.name: MCP Flight Recorder
nodes.description: A CI-native scanner and out-of-band flight recorder for the Model Context Protocol — capturing agent tool calls, identities, data access, tool versions, and side effects as an evidence trail, so what an autonomous agent did can be reconstructed after the fact.

nodes.name: Progressive Insurance
nodes.description: Engineered NLP and computer-vision models using TensorFlow and PyTorch to classify claim texts, forms, and images. Built ML pipelines with Apache Airflow and Azure Data Factory, deployed to Azure ML Services — 35% reduction in manual claim processing time, 25% improvement in fraud detection.

nodes.name: Indiana University
nodes.description: Improved transcript accuracy by 18 percentage points using a GPT-4 RAG pipeline on the BigRed200 HPC cluster, processing 200+ hours of esports video. Cut chat latency 40% with a sentiment microservice handling 1M+ messages in near real time.

nodes.name: IBM
nodes.description: Led churn prediction model development in Python and Scikit-learn — 20% reduction in customer attrition. Refactored ETL workflows with Azure Data Lake and SQL for 15% faster data availability, and shipped models to Azure ML behind CI/CD for 25% faster releases.

Two parallel first passes at retrieval in 2024 — the same embed/index/retrieve pattern, once in notebooks and once behind a Streamlit UI.
Single-document retrieval grew into a production-shaped hybrid pipeline — keyword, vector, and authority signals ranked together over a real corpus.
The notebook retrieval experiments became the retrieval stage of an eight-agent workflow.
The litigation-agent demo's orchestration and evidence handling became the foundation of a production legal-tech product.
Both expose their capabilities as MCP tools so an external agent can drive them — one for job applications, one for litigation work.

Graph analysis moved from a private social export to a public, citation-backed dataset built for other people to explore.
Two productizations of the same upstream swarm engine — one as a metered prediction API, one as a go-to-market simulation lab.
